headline: SUPER MARIO takes the WATCH seat — and the rollout closes
lede: b31 audited every unseated title on the shelf for a proven winning driver, found exactly one (Mario's certified autopilot), seated it with the flagpole-completes-the-watcher law — and pinned the honest remainder so no unproven title can ever grow a silent button.

notes.text: Press Y on Super Mario Bros and the machine that autopilotcheck certifies — flagpole, all lives, zero deaths — takes the overalls on World 1-1. Any key, click or tap hands them back mid-sector with clean keys.

The audit ledger: the nine titles without a proven driver (Pac-Man, Centipede, Pitfall, IronKeep, Britannia, Zork II/III, Mario Classic, Raccoon Heist) stay honest with no guide — and a watchcheck pin now fails CI if any of them ever advertises WATCH.

A mode flip is not a handback: the first flagpole release left the autopilot's held run-key behind, and World 1-3 started with a stuck run button — Mario walk-ran into a firebar three times with zero player input. release() now cleans keys, and the pin says exactly why.
git stash is repo-wide across worktrees: a pop landed another lane's stash into my tree mid-session. Recovery via reset --hard (the stash survived); the playbook lesson: checkpoint with commits only.

look.text: Watch Mario clear 1-1 perfectly — then grab the overalls mid-sector
